_comment: Ratchet baselines for checks/run.js. Baselines only move toward the target, with the reason recorded in the PR that moves them. allowedExternalPrefixes is EMPTY and stays empty: since S5 the game embeds its own fonts and references nothing off-origin (invariant 4).
_mathRandomComment: S3 routed all 93 call sites through the seeded engine. The one that remains is rand()'s own pre-game fallback, for the window before S exists where there is nothing to be reproducible about. The sandbox's Math.random swap is an assignment, not a call, so it does not count here — it stays as isolation for any stray call this file grows later. A rise means a new unseeded source of randomness: route it through rand() instead.
_sizeComment: S9g moved this 1,600,000 -> 1,750,000, S9h -> 1,900,000, S10a -> 2,100,000. The binding invariant is self-containment, not bytes: one file, no build step, no external reference, opens from file://. The ratchet exists to catch growth nobody decided on, and every move here was decided on. S9g: twenty-four statutes in each of the twenty core categories (131 new, 95 KB). S9h: four authored rungs on the 451 statutes that were already here (167 KB). S10a: raised BEFORE the work that needs it rather than after, because the owner's fifth order includes a book of at least 36 executive orders, roughly 32 new grand works, and expanded material for Question Time and the political papers — an estimated 135-150 KB — and discovering the ceiling midway through that would mean content authored and unable to land. Headroom stays deliberately finite so the ratchet still bites on anything unplanned. S10g: -> 2,200,000. The tail of the S10f authoring run rewrote eighteen shards AFTER the first seventy questions had been merged and shipped, leaving forty-five more on disk that no build had seen; levelling the five subjects that had been left shallow adds twenty-five more. Ninety-two KB of authored question, taking Question Time from five sentences in an if/else chain to a hundred and sixty-four questions, twelve on every one of its fourteen subjects. The owner's ninth item was 'expand or remove'; this is the expansion, and it is the last of it. Headroom stays deliberately finite so the ratchet still bites on anything unplanned. S11g/S11a: -> 2,450,000, raised BEFORE the sixth order is authored rather than after, the way S10a did it. The order carries twenty charts and their recorder, thirty-six more executive orders (measured at 629 bytes each, so ≈23 KB), roughly forty constitutional articles, a rebuilt Federation model and two rebuilt tabs — an estimated 150-200 KB against 38 KB of headroom. Discovering the ceiling midway through would mean authored content that cannot land, which is the failure this ratchet's own history says to avoid. Headroom stays deliberately finite so the check still bites on anything nobody decided on. | S12 raises it 2,450,000 -> 3,000,000 for the statute book's prose: 582 statutes x 4 rungs is 2,328 descriptions at a mean of about 230 chars (535 KB), plus ~29 KB of array structure, plus ~32 KB net for the 582 refreshed desc lines (they total 61 KB today at a median of 76 chars). Roughly 600 KB against 119,583 of headroom, so the move happens BEFORE the authoring rather than after, or finished content strands. Projected final is near 2,930,000, which leaves the ratchet about 70 KB of bite. The prose is static registry data: POLICIES is a top-level literal, not serialised, not in UI.undoStack and not inside v6Sandbox's clone, so none of this reaches a save, an undo frame or a forecast.
_tiersComment: S6a collapsed 13 accreted width thresholds to these five, one per tier edge plus the small-phone refinement the user sanctioned. Six chunks each picking its own 'narrow' number is how the tablet band ended up half-dressed, so a new threshold fails this check. Adding one is a design decision: make the case in the PR, then add the number here.
_heightComment: The one height threshold in the file: the landscape/short-window turn bar. It was governed by nothing until the breakpoint check learned about the height axis.
_tenthComment: S9d added the v10 Descent chunk (7->8): the engine that makes the descent roads real. The case is in PR #19; the chunk defines no ensure function and never wraps enrichState, so the S3 dice guard stays outermost.
